subject.title: Gateway boot: no observability for subsystem startup failures (gmail-watcher, hooks)

question: What stable Gateway boot-summary contract should OpenClaw expose for startup sidecars and hooks, including Gmail watcher skipped reasons?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but subsystem scope, fixed reason strings, and scheduled-versus-started wording create user-visible operations behavior that automation should not define alone.

options.title: Approve narrow fixed-vocabulary summary
options.body: Add one redacted startup outcome line for Gateway-owned sidecars and hooks, including Gmail watcher skipped reasons, with tests proving no secrets or raw details are logged.

options.title: Limit to Gmail watcher diagnostics
options.body: Only surface Gmail watcher skipped reasons now and defer broader subsystem startup reporting to a later diagnostics design.

options.title: Defer to diagnostics commands
options.body: Keep startup logs compact and require operators to use health, status, or diagnostics commands for subsystem startup state.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow fixed-vocabulary summary
recommendation.body: Add one redacted startup outcome line for Gateway-owned sidecars and hooks, including Gmail watcher skipped reasons, with tests proving no secrets or raw details are logged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history across the Gmail lifecycle helper plus prior issue analysis for this exact Gateway startup/logging decision.
